newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-BARCELONA INTO SEMIFINAL AFTER AIK DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA INTO SEMIFINAL AFTER AIK DRAW.

text.p: A 12th minute strike from Brazilian forward Ronaldo was enough to steer Barcelona into the semifinals of the Cup Winners Cup as they drew 1-1 at AIK Stockholm on Thursday to take the tie 4-2 on aggregate.
Freezing temperatures of minus four degrees Celsius, at Stockholm's Rasunda stadium failed to inhibit the Spaniards, who quickly added to their 3-1 first-leg lead.

Ronaldo lived up to the high expectations of the 35,000 crowd when he scored an early textbook goal, receiving a well-timed pass from Bulgarian international Hristo Stoichkov and driving his shot into the roof of the net.
The Spaniards continued to press throughout the first half as Stoichkov and Ivan de la Pena ran the game from midfield.
After the game, Barcelona coach Bobby Robson said he was disappointed that his side failed to get the second goal when they were on top and go on to win the game.
"Barcelona controlled the match for 70 minutes. We should have made a second goal and killed the game," he said.
"We would have won the game by two to three goals if the last passes had been better."
But it was AIK who adopted more aggressive tactics in the second half and equalised in the 75th minute through Pascal Simpson, their goalscorer in the first leg a fortnight ago.
The goal rejuvenated AIK, with Johan Mjallby making an effective move from defence into midfield, but despite two near attempts they could not overturn Barcelona's advantage.
"We took a step back in the first half instead of putting pressure on Barcelona's players," AIK coach Eric Hemren said.
But it was Simpson who correctly summed up the difference between the two sides.
"It was good to score again against Barcelona but we weren't good enough today," he said.
